html:
The account has now made it through one full calendar year: 2020.

This year we published 28 articles, four more than the 24 we projected last year. Besides Er Mu and Fanyu, six new authors joined us.

Follower numbers


As of the evening of December 30, 2020, we had 6,673 followers in total, up 4,923 on last year. That falls short of the five figures we hoped for in last year’s review, but for a niche field like acoustics it’s respectable enough.

In September, with our first followers in Tibet and Qinghai, the account finally reached every province across mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan. By region, the top three are Guangdong, Beijing and Shanghai.

Back in September there were five. As for the four who unfollowed, we need to talk ->_->

The share of women rose from 23.03% last year to 24.73% this year. The number of followers of unknown gender showed no growth.

By age, people aged 26–35 are by far our core readership, close to 50%.

The share of overseas Chinese also grew significantly this year. Language settings don’t capture all of our overseas followers, but the figure is clearly up on last year.


Content numbers

WeChat only shows content statistics for the last three months; seeing the full history apparently takes a web scraper. Over the last three months, our articles were read 28,000 times and shared 1,587 times in total.

The three most-read articles were:

What is acoustics?

Everything you wanted to know about noise-cancelling headphones, part 1

Into acoustics: a tour of Europe’s best-known acoustics labs

Acoustics is a small branch of physics, but it is becoming more and more interdisciplinary. When sound meets buildings, you get architectural acoustics. To understand how sound travels in the sea, you turn to ocean acoustics. The study of how people subjectively perceive sound is psychoacoustics. And acoustics has spawned many more subfields: electroacoustics, bioacoustics, environmental acoustics, musical acoustics and so on.

Doing acoustics outreach well really takes knowledge collectors from each of these subfields sharing their insights. In a difficult 2020, the account was lucky to welcome authors from different corners of acoustics: Acoustics PhD, a One Piece fan who explains ultrasound diagnostics; Dr. Like Jiang, who puts a price on traffic noise; S.Li, who shares know-how on active noise cancellation; Dr. Xuhao Du, who works on medical acoustics; jemand, who looks at acoustic metamaterials from a condensed-matter angle; and Dr. Yiying Hao, who takes aircraft noise apart. We are truly grateful to them for joining us and sharing their expertise.

To write a good popular-science article, you need the relevant expertise, of course, but perhaps the other key ingredient is liking it: liking doing this kind of thing and believing it’s worth doing. We and the six people above all have our own day jobs or studies. We come from all over China and are scattered across the country and abroad, and it is precisely because we like and believe in this work that, alongside busy jobs and studies, we keep dreaming up and writing one article after another.

Zhan Qingyun, a debater on the Chinese debate show Qipa Shuo (U Can U BIBI), once talked on the show about “the power of liking something”: liking leads to creating, and creating leads to things of value. In 2021, besides hoping we can finally take off our masks, we also hope that acoustics enthusiasts from every field who like and value this little thing we do will join us and share the knowledge, opinions and even fun stories about acoustics they have collected. Join our authors’ group, too, where you can talk freely with people from different fields, online and offline, and strike a few sparks.

We don’t really know how long we’ll keep doing this little thing, where this account will end up, or how many people will read our articles in the end. But when we see comments like “I’m studying xxx and got started with your xxx article, thanks for sharing” or “My child is learning to play xx, great article,” we feel what this little thing is worth. Maybe much of the time there’s no such feedback on its “value.” Whatever happens, in the words of the great Luo Yonghao, pioneer of Chinese stand-up and one of the country’s original internet celebrities: let’s make friends!

And finally, of course, our New Year wishes!

In the new year, we hope you’ll all:

Take off your masks!

Stay healthy!!

Be happy!!!

Get younger every year!!!!

— Fanyu and Er Mu

Oh, and speaking of which, our author friends have sent in their greetings too. Let’s see what they have to say. Over to the big screen!

Like Jiang (University of Leeds, urban transport and environmental noise):

About a year and a half ago, I read a Ziyu Acoustics post for the first time (I think it was the one on architectural acoustics). On the one hand, I thought how great it would have been to have reading like this, easygoing yet professional, back when I was an urban-planning student just getting into acoustics. On the other, I marveled that spending your free time writing and compiling these articles really takes a heart that loves acoustics. And after I had the honor of writing a post for Ziyu Acoustics myself, I appreciated even more how hard it is. The style may look relaxed, but every figure and every claim in these posts is written down only when it’s well sourced and the authors are completely sure of it. Writing a popular-science post isn’t easy; running a popular-science account is harder still. I hope Ziyu Acoustics keeps getting better in the new year and brings acoustics professionals and enthusiasts more high-quality, fun acoustics outreach!

Yiying Hao (senior engineer, Bureau Veritas, Manchester; PhD and postdoc in architecture, University of Sheffield):

Zeno said that human knowledge is like a circle: inside the circle is what we know, outside it what we don’t. The more you know, the bigger the circle, and the more you don’t know. Ziyu Acoustics is an account that keeps drawing that circle bigger in the niche field of acoustics. As a reader, I enjoy every moment of discovery the articles bring; as an author, I’m moved by the passion and perseverance of its two young editors. Here’s to growing together with Ziyu Acoustics in 2021!

S.Li (an acoustics PhD student who has been wandering around Germany for years):

Thanks to Fanyu for inviting me to write popular-science articles for the account, and thanks for having a platform like this where I can share what I’ve learned about acoustics~ I hope we can all keep talking and exchanging ideas. 2020 is almost over. This year I dawdled my way through three articles; next year I hope to keep it up and stop procrastinating! And to finish my PhD without a hitch.

Xuhao Du (PhD in acoustics, University of Western Australia; formerly a postdoc in Nobel laureate Barry Marshall’s lab):

Ziyu Acoustics is the most comprehensive acoustics outreach platform I’ve seen in the field! I’m lucky to be able to talk with everyone here through my articles, and I hope that next year we can explore together even more of the strange sounds the human body makes!

jemand (BSc in physics, Nanjing University; currently studying for an MSc in physics at RWTH Aachen University):

This is the present writer’s first contribution to a public platform. As a newcomer who has only just switched to acoustics, a field still largely unknown to me, writing an introductory article felt rather like showing off one’s axe at the master carpenter’s door, and I wrote it with great care. Thanks to the kindness of my two seniors, Fanyu and Er Mu, and of the readers, the article was published and drew a respectable number of reads. My heartfelt thanks to the two of them for providing such an excellent platform, where I can exchange knowledge of acoustics with so many experts. In fact, the reason I chose Aachen as my next step was reading Fanyu’s articles. From them I learned that besides physical acoustics, Nanjing University’s strength, there are new and intriguing ideas and directions such as psychoacoustics and virtual acoustics, and I learned about RWTH Aachen, TUM and a host of other excellent European acoustics research institutions. Having met my Waterloo in condensed matter physics, I believe my decision to switch fields was right and that I will achieve something in acoustics, and much of that confidence comes from the articles my seniors have published here. As we ring out the old and ring in the new, I wish all my seniors and readers good health in the new year (that’s the most important thing), success in your careers and happiness in your families, and I wish Ziyu Acoustics ever greater success ;)
